name: task-row
title: Task row
description: A task as a list row: checkbox, title, due date in words, assignee, priority mark and subtask count.
docs: Put the rows in a ul. task is { id, title, href, done, completedAt, due, assignee, subtasks, priority }; the due date comes from DueDateLabel, so a date-only string such as "2026-10-28" is a calendar day and the words are Due today, Due tomorrow, Due in 5 days and Overdue by 2 days, with an icon and weight as well as colour. onToggle receives the state the checkbox asks for: update task.done, and set completedAt to have a finished task say Done on 12 Oct. The checkbox is its own control and never opens the task; completing it strikes the title and says Completed to screen readers. The rest of the row is one link (task.href) or button (onOpen) under the checkbox and the actions slot. A long title stays on one line in a wide row and takes up to two in a narrow one; the whole of it appears in a tooltip on hover and keyboard focus. selected marks the task whose details are open with a bar and aria-current; density="compact" tightens the rows. The row follows its own width: from 36rem everything sits on one line in fixed columns, below that the details wrap under the title. Pass now for deterministic due dates in tests and previews. Give the actions a group-hover/task-row class to reveal them on hover.
